clue.text: One learning in class to make a defensive move

indicators.note: in tells us the learner's letter sits inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a social class
L stands for a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A pupil in a classroom learns how to protect themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: To castle is a chess move that tucks the king safely behind a rook.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, castling is a manoeuvre that shelters the king, a protective play.

clue.text: Restrict prisoners with chain

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts
a train is a connected series, a chain

explanation.surface: Inmates are kept in check by being shackled.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to limit or hold back, which is what restricting does.

clue.text: Ensured clean, fine wood

parts.note: saw, as in saw to it, means made sure
to dust is to clean

explanation.surface: Someone made sure that fine timber was wiped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine wood' is not quality timber but wood in fine particles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawdust is timber reduced to tiny particles by cutting.

clue.text: Most insignificant point in final

indicators.note: in says the compass point goes inside the word for final

parts.note: last means final
E is a point of the compass, east

explanation.surface: The smallest detail is in the final stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, so smallest or of lowest importance.

clue.text: Variety of bee, plain and common

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes an ordinary, unremarkable kind of bee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges BEE and PLAIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian describes the ordinary people, the lower orders, hence ordinary or vulgar.

clue.text: Autobiography of Hood's man, in small instalments

definitions.meaning: Robin Hood's man is Little John, so his own life story would be titled by its author as by Little
gradually, a bit at a time

explanation.surface: A member of Robin Hood's band writes his memoirs, published bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood's outlaw companion is Little John: a book about Little written by Little.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means gradually, step by step, in tiny amounts.

clue.text: Cover county — tramp round about

parts.note: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: round says the word for tramp surrounds the word for about

parts.note: to pad is to tramp along on foot
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A hobo hides himself in a shire somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is an English county north of London, abbreviated Beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is the decorative top layer laid over a bed.

clue.text: Time's up" can be such an incentive

indicators.note: can be says these letters may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Being told the time has run out spurs people on.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is a driving force, motivation, a spur to act.

clue.text: Dapper Bumppo

definitions.meaning: ... Bumppo is the frontiersman hero of Fenimore Cooper's Leatherstocking novels

explanation.definitionFit: The word means smartly dressed, and it is also the first name of Cooper's scout.

clue.text: Having foolishly taken the coins put myself in tricky situation

indicators.note: foolishly means the words are mixed up in a silly way

explanation.surface: Having stupidly pocketed the money, the speaker is now in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges TAKEN THE COINS with I.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture onto risky ground is to take a dangerous chance, as on fragile frozen water.

clue.text: Fresh outlet for game

parts.note: fresh means new
a market is an outlet for selling goods

explanation.surface: A new shop opens selling venison and other game.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is a card game; it is also a Suffolk town famous for horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is the name of a betting card game, so it is one example of a pastime.

clue.text: Some low-grade potatoes in store

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A warehouse is holding a stock of poor-quality spuds.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse or warehouse; the clue phrase works as a noun phrase meaning a place for storing.

clue.text: Twit getting tight about noon \

indicators.note: about means the word for tight goes around the letter for noon

parts.note: taut means pulled tight

explanation.surface: A foolish person gets drunk around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twit' looks like a noun for a fool but is the verb, to tease; 'tight' tempts as drunk but means TAUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To twit someone is to tease or mock them, a synonym for jeer.

clue.text: They leapt all over the place, establishing channel of communication

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, so the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Creatures leap about wildly, opening a line of contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathy is supposed mind-to-mind contact, a means of passing thoughts without speech.

clue.text: Darts player finally aims thus quickly

definitions.meaning: a darts game must end on a double, so the player's last throw is aimed at that ring
a military phrase for running pace, hence fast

explanation.surface: A darts player takes aim at the end of a match without wasting time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a drill order for a fast running pace, so it means hurriedly.

clue.text: Improve on yarn to do needlework

definitions.meaning: to add fanciful details to a story or tale
to decorate fabric with stitched patterns

explanation.surface: Someone adds to the wool to make some sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like wool for sewing, but is a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: One embellishes a story with invented detail, and also decorates cloth with stitched designs.

clue.text: Dark blue

definitions.meaning: an old sense of the word describes a deep, sombre colour

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: archaically a dull dark colour, and in everyday use unhappy, feeling low.

clue.text: Record about unknown finding

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means about, as in argue over
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A record of the unknown is uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found, such as a new fact or find.

clue.text: God goes back down

indicators.note: goes back says the god's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A deity returns to the earth below.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap is the soft raised pile on cloth, much like down, the fluffy feathers.

clue.text: Try embracing good cause

indicators.note: embracing says the word for try holds the word for good inside

parts.note: to prove, as in proving a will, is to test or try
OK means good, acceptable

explanation.surface: An attempt to hug someone is a good thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke something is to bring it about, to give rise to it.

clue.text: It could be Albert's, Ted's or Tommy's clothing

indicators.note: it could be says the letters of the names may be rearranged into the answer

parts.note: taken with its S as written
taken with its S as written

explanation.surface: Some garment might belong to one of three men, Albert, Ted or Tommy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be' rearranges ALBERTS and TEDS; 'or' just joins. Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is old slang for a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tommy is a British soldier, and battledress is the soldier's field uniform.

clue.text: Former partner greeting part in show

parts.note: ex is a former spouse or partner
hi is a greeting
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse says hello at a theatre performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibit is something put on display, and to exhibit is to display.

clue.text: Champion has a game point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A sports champion holds the deciding point in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is not a winner here but one who argues for a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who defends a belief in argument is its champion or advocate.

clue.text: Look for a singer

parts.note: waits were bands of street singers performing carols at Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Waits are a British tradition of carol singers going door to door at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to expect it, to look forward to its arrival.

clue.text: Brutish creature responsible for return of crop circles

indicators.note: return means the word for crop is turned backwards

parts.note: hay is a crop of grass
O looks like a circle, so two circles are OO

explanation.surface: A thug is blamed for the mysterious crop circles in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns HAY into YAH. Yahoos are the bestial humans in Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: In Swift the Yahoos are degraded humanlike brutes, so the word means a boorish lout.

clue.text: Incredible sort of flying you often got in Concorde originally

indicators.note: originally says take the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Concorde passengers often had an amazing flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Yogic flying is a meditation practice of hopping cross-legged, claimed to be levitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogic flying is a cross-legged bouncing claimed as levitation through meditation, an unbelievable kind of flight.

clue.text: Permitted to speak so as to be heard

indicators.note: to speak says the word for permitted is to be said out loud

parts.note: allowed means permitted

explanation.surface: Someone is given leave to talk so everyone can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something audibly means voicing it for others to hear.

clue.text: I will say Bible's not first book that's unreadable

parts.note: eg (for example) means say

indicators.note: not first says the opening letter is dropped from the Holy Book

parts.note: the Bible, with 's read as has

explanation.surface: Someone admits that the first book of the Bible is impossible to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not first' takes the B (book) off BIBLE, leaving IBLE; 'that's' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegible writing cannot be deciphered, the same as unreadable text.

clue.text: Conjectures and experiments involving helium and oxygen

indicators.note: involving means the trials wrap around the two element symbols

parts.note: tries are attempts or experiments
He is the chemical symbol for helium
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A scientist makes guesses and runs tests with two gases.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are hypotheses, speculative explanations not yet proven.

clue.text: Dizzy pet put in animals' home

indicators.note: put in says the pet's letters go inside the home

parts.note: a sty is a home for pigs
a cat is a pet

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained pet is sent to a rescue shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animals' home' suggests a shelter, but it is a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty means scatterbrained, flighty, absent-minded.
